answer: Sybils fail when a new key's attestations stay weightless until bonded stake has aged through a fixed multi-epoch unlock delay. A factory can wander from alias to alias, yet each alias still freezes coins, and an early unbond slashes the bond. The remaining delay is posted as a short cipher any rater can recompute against the ledger, so cloned keys cannot buy influence overnight. That aged bond is the yarrow in the field: a small, specific marker that real participants already paid for.
